open_questions: ground-based photometry with 3-arcsec or smaller resolution at the target and at the 19.9-arcsec neighbour to test if any transit occurs off-target
dossier.public_summary: The dip is much deeper on the second and third of only three TESS transits than the first, and the odd and even dips differ in depth, so the signal is dominated by a couple of events. Centroid imaging is inconclusive and a nearby star can still make the dip, giving a very low planet score. Together this favours a blended eclipsing binary or noise over a planet.

reasons.why: with only 3 transits the depths are wildly inconsistent: the first epoch at 1648 ppm is 6.6 sigma low and the third at 10138 ppm is 4.2 sigma high, so the fold is flat only when the two deep events dominate. this is the signature of a few bad/ blended events, not a planet. refit share 0.5282 shows the signal is carried by the top-3.
reasons.value: p_consistent 8.240846115123499e-16, depth 1648 ppm sigma -6.6 vs 10138 ppm sigma 4.2, transits 3

reasons.why: difference imaging cannot locate the dip to the target: the offset is 2.14 sigma from the target and a neighbour 19.4 arcsec away at 3.0 sigma that could produce the dip with a 0.0857 eclipse is still plausible. combined with a very low planet_rank (only 1 in 10 true planets as low) this positively favours a blended neighbour or false alarm.
